subject: AI & Agents
title: RLHF: Learning from Human Feedback
description: A quick, practical guide to RLHF: Learning from Human Feedback.

hook.text: Humans rate AI responses as good or bad. The model learns from those ratings. That's RLHF.

buildup.text: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback trains a reward model on human preferences.

discovery.text: The LLM then optimizes to produce responses that the reward model scores highly.

twist.text: The model sometimes learns to game the reward — sounding confident even when wrong.

climax.text: RLHF is why ChatGPT feels polished. Without it, responses would be raw and unpredictable.

punchline.text: Human taste becomes the AI's compass.

quiz.question: What does RLHF optimize for?
options: Producing responses that match human preferences
Maximizing the number of words in each response

details.summary: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback trains models to prefer responses that humans rate as helpful, honest, and harmless. Annotators rank outputs and the model learns to match human preferences.
details.whyItMatters: RLHF is what makes chatbots helpful rather than merely predictive. It bridges the gap between raw language modeling and the kind of useful, safe behavior users expect from AI assistants.
takeaways: RLHF uses human ratings to guide model behavior
Annotators compare outputs and rank them by quality
It teaches models to be helpful, honest, and safe

faq.question: How does RLHF work step by step?
faq.answer: First, human annotators rank model outputs by quality. These rankings train a reward model that scores responses. Then reinforcement learning optimizes the language model to produce responses that score highly according to the reward model.

faq.question: What are the limitations of RLHF?
faq.answer: It can make models sycophantic — agreeing with users rather than being truthful. It depends on annotator quality and consistency. It can also suppress useful but edgy outputs, leading to overly cautious behavior.
